City of Armadale
Armadale, Perth WA
Engineering – Civil/Structural Engineering 
$102,000–$117,000 per annum plus superannuation
Shape a growing City’s infrastructure. Plan capital projects through design, costing and approvals, with WFH and flexi-time for a 9-day fortnight.
 -  Shape infrastructure projects across asset renewal, upgrades and growth.
 -  Flexible working with WFH and accrued flexi-time towards a 9-day fortnight.
 -  Superannuation up to 15%, subject to conditions, plus free gym membership.
 Help shape the projects that shape our City
Good infrastructure starts with good decisions. Understanding what is needed, testing the options and resolving the detail before construction begins.
At the City of Armadale, you’ll help make those decisions. As one of Western Australia’s fastest-growing local governments, we’re planning new infrastructure while improving and renewing the assets our community already relies on.
We’re looking for a Project Planning Engineer who brings practical judgement, asks good questions and takes pride in preparing projects properly.
If you’re enjoying your current role but would welcome the opportunity to influence a growing City’s infrastructure, this could be your next move.
Why Armadale?
Our Strategic Community Plan sets a clear direction: facilities that meet community needs, better public places, and infrastructure that is functional, inclusive and sustainable.
You’ll help turn those priorities into practical projects, balancing technical requirements, cost, risk and long-term asset performance. Across renewal, upgrade and growth projects, you’ll tackle varied challenges and see how your work contributes to the community.
You’ll also have flexibility in how you work, including working from home and the ability to accrue flexi-time to work a nine-day fortnight, with arrangements agreed around role and team requirements.
Your role
Working in our Asset Planning team, reporting to the Project Planning Lead, you’ll progress identified infrastructure priorities into well-defined, costed and approved capital projects ready for delivery.
Starting with Project Initiation Documents developed by Strategic Asset Management, you’ll coordinate investigations and detailed designs, refine cost estimates and progress the approvals needed for capital works program entry.
You’ll work with engineering and landscape design specialists, consultants, asset operators and delivery teams to:
 - Develop clear project scopes, specifications and budget requirements.
 - Coordinate investigations, technical advice and detailed design activities.
 - Prepare and refine cost estimates, checking assumptions, contingencies and constructability.
 - Progress approvals, utility clearances, statutory consents and other project requirements.
 - Prepare complete project packages for review under the City’s Project Management Framework.
 - Resolve risks and gaps early, considering procurement, construction sequencing and handover requirements.
Your work will help the City make informed investment decisions and give delivery teams confidence in each project’s scope, cost and readiness.
What you’ll bring
You know what it takes to prepare an infrastructure project for delivery. You can work through technical detail, challenge assumptions constructively and bring the right people together to resolve issues.
We’re looking for:
 - Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering, Project Management, Construction Management or a closely related discipline**, or equivalent demonstrated experience in project planning and infrastructure development.
 - Experience planning civil infrastructure or construction projects.
 - Sound knowledge of cost estimation, contingency allowances and key cost drivers.
 - The ability to coordinate technical input across disciplines and progress third-party approvals.
 - Familiarity with project management frameworks and project approval requirements.
Flexibility and benefits
 - Working-from-home arrangements and flexi-time, including the ability to accrue time towards a nine-day fortnight.
 - Superannuation contributions of up to 15%, subject to employee contributions and applicable conditions.
 - Free Armadale Fitness and Aquatic Centre membership**, including the gym, pools, sauna and group fitness classes.
 - Wellbeing activities throughout the year.
 - Novated leasing opportunities.
Our values—Care; Are Better, Together; Learn & Grow; and Seize Today, Shape Tomorrow—guide how we work. We listen, share knowledge and welcome people who bring ideas and take responsibility for their work.
Interested? Let’s talk
You don’t need to be actively looking for a new job to explore this opportunity.
For an initial confidential conversation, contact People Services on 9394 5189 or hr@armadale.wa.gov.au. 
Ready to apply? Submit your CV and a brief cover letter through the application link, outlining your relevant experience and interest in the role.
We review applications as they are received and may close the advertisement early.
*The City of Armadale welcomes applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, people from culturally diverse backgrounds and people of all genders and identities.*
*We are committed to child safety and recruitment practices that support a safe and inclusive community.*

Help shape stormwater’s next chapter.

We’re a specialist stormwater and surface water consultancy. We plan and design better water environments, investigate how water behaves and help clients turn complex information into decisions they can act on.
Our purpose
At Rain, we exist to support, challenge and lift ourselves, each other and the people we work with.
That means helping clients understand their options and giving them the clarity and confidence to act. It also means backing our own people to develop their judgement, take ownership and contribute to how the industry works.
We value creative thinking, especially when it leads to a sound, practical solution.
How we work
Our values guide our decisions and the standards we hold ourselves to:
- Quality: We check assumptions, review our work and explain the findings clearly.
- Integrity: We give honest advice, including when a client needs to hear something difficult.
- Stewardship: We consider what our decisions mean for communities and the environment over the long term.
You’ll work with major clients, including City of Melbourne and Melbourne Water, as part of a small team where your contribution is visible.
You’ll have direct support from Luke and Rianda, Rain’s Directors, and colleagues who want to see you develop. As your capability grows, there’s room to take on greater responsibility and build your own voice in the industry.
We welcome questions, thoughtful challenges and ideas for doing things better. You’ll be trusted to contribute, with technical review and support around you.
The role is Melbourne-based with hybrid working and flexibility, within a team that looks out for each other.
The problems you’ll help solve
A council is rethinking how it manages water across its community. A wetland or waterway needs a design that supports both people and the environment. A project needs a water balance to understand where water comes from, where it goes and how it could be used.
And behind each challenge, there are people who need help turning complex information into a clear way forward.
These are the kinds of questions you’ll work through at Rain.
You’ll use TUFLOW and RORB to investigate how water behaves, test options and understand their consequences. Your projects may also involve wetland and waterway design, water balances and integrated water management. You’ll turn that work into clear maps, reports and conversations that help people make sound decisions.
You’ll also get involved beyond the technical analysis. From shaping the brief to discussing the findings with the client, you’ll develop an understanding of what makes a project useful, achievable and worth doing. That includes managing scope, budgets and deadlines, with support from the team.
We want you to question assumptions and contribute ideas. If you see a better way to approach a problem, explain a result or manage water, there’s room to explore it with us.
As your confidence and capability grow, you’ll have opportunities to take greater ownership, guide others and contribute to our training or facilitation work.
The aim is for your contribution to keep helping people long after the report is delivered.
What you’ll bring
- An Engineering degree, including civil or environmental engineering, or an Environmental Science degree.
- 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience in flood, stormwater or water management.
- Solid practical TUFLOW and RORB skills.
- An understanding of hydrologic, hydraulic and stormwater processes.
- The ability to plan your work, take responsibility and ask for support when you need it.
- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical findings to different audiences.
- Curiosity about better ways of doing things and care for the quality and impact of your work.
Experience with MUSIC and QGIS is valuable. Training, facilitation or mentoring experience is a bonus.
Your next move
Send your CV and a short note about why you’d like to work at Rain to hiring@rainconsulting.com.au.
Tell us about the work you’ve done, the work you’d like to do next and what you’d bring to the team.
You’re also welcome to email us if you’d like to ask a question before applying.
We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds and experiences.
